Apply SRTR factor labels to a data frame

Source: R/apply_srtr_factors.R
apply_srtr_factors.Rd

Converts coded variables in an SRTR dataset into human-readable factors using the SRTR data dictionary and associated format tables.

Usage

apply_srtr_factors(
  df,
  file_key = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  range_formats = c("keep", "bin"),
  unknown_codes = c("keep", "na", "error"),
  other = c("sas", "keep"),
  release = NULL
)

Arguments

df

A data frame loaded from an SRTR SAF file.

file_key

Optional. The dataset name (e.g., "CAND_KIPA", "TX_KI"). If not provided, the function will use a file_key attribute or object name.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, print each variable being labeled.

range_formats

What to do with numeric variables whose format is a set of bands rather than a code list: the age formats AGE8A, AGE8C and AGE9A, used by REC_AGE_AT_TX and CAN_AGE_AT_LISTING. "keep" (the default) leaves the numbers as they are. "bin" turns them into a factor of bands. The page lists only each band's lower bound, so "bin" treats each listed code as the start of a band that runs to the next one; this reading is a convention, not stated by SRTR.

unknown_codes

What to do with a value that is not a code in the variable's format (and is not covered by a catch-all entry, see other). "keep" (the default) keeps it as an extra level named by the raw code followed by ": not in format", so it cannot be mistaken for a label; "na" turns it into NA. Both warn (class sRtr_warning_unknown_codes). "error" stops (class sRtr_error_unknown_codes).

other

What to do with a format's catch-all entry (**OTHER**, as in RACE, where it means "Multi-Racial"). "sas" (the default) gives every value not otherwise listed the catch-all label, as a SAS format does. "keep" ignores the catch-all, so those values are handled by unknown_codes.

release

Optional. The SAF release df comes from, as year and month ("2609"), to use that release's dictionary and formats (see srtr_dictionary()). If NULL (the default), the release recorded by load_srtr_file() is used, or the bundled dictionary and formats if there is none.

Value

A data frame with factor levels applied to coded variables, and a file_key attribute holding the dataset key in upper case, so the key carries through a chain of calls. If no usable key is found, df is returned unchanged with a warning.

Details

If file_key is not explicitly provided, the function will first check for a file_key attribute on the data frame (e.g., from load_srtr_file()). If not found, it will attempt to infer it from the object name.

The key is matched in upper case. A key that is not a dataset in the bundled dictionary, or a key that cannot be worked out (no attribute and no object name, as when df is an expression), gives a warning. A known key whose columns are not in df is not a problem: nothing is changed.

Values are read as codes. A value that is not a code in the format is outside it, even if it reads like one of the format's labels.

A column converted by an earlier call carries an srtr_format attribute and is left as it is, so calling the function twice changes nothing. dplyr and tibble operations keep the attribute; base R subsetting such as df[rows, ] on a data frame drops it, and the column is then read as codes again, with every value reported as outside the format (also when the format has a catch-all: for a factor input, values given the catch-all label are reported too; raw codes get it silently, as in SAS). Convert again from the raw codes, or keep working with dplyr. Attributes on each column, such as a variable label, are kept.

When codes that are not in the format are kept, the column also carries an srtr_kept_codes attribute: a named vector giving, for each such level, the original code. srtr_missing_report() uses it to recognise those codes after labelling.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Explicit file_key
df <- read_sas("TX_KI.sas7bdat")
df <- apply_srtr_factors(df, file_key = "TX_KI", verbose = TRUE)

# Implicit file_key from attribute (if loaded via load_srtr_file)
df <- load_srtr_file("TX_KI")
df <- apply_srtr_factors(df)

# Fallback to object name inference
TX_KI <- read_sas("TX_KI.sas7bdat")
TX_KI <- apply_srtr_factors(TX_KI)
} # }
